definitions.explanation: Vessels and objects made from clay and fired in a kiln. In the strict sense, refers to earthenware (fired at lower temperatures, somewhat porous) as opposed to porcelain (磁器), but in common usage can refer to ceramics in general.

examples.japanese: この{陶器|とうき}は{手作|てづく}りだ。
{陶器|とうき}{市|いち}で{気|き}に{入|い}った{茶碗|ちゃわん}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought a rice bowl I liked at the pottery market.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}には{有田焼|ありたやき}や{備前焼|びぜんやき}など{有名|ゆうめい}な{陶器|とうき}の{産地|さんち}がたくさんある。
examples.english: Japan has many famous pottery production areas, such as Arita ware and Bizen ware.

notes:
Compound of {陶|とう} (pottery/clay) + {器|き} (vessel/utensil).

Strictly speaking, {陶器|とうき} (earthenware) and {磁器|じき} (porcelain) are different: {陶器|とうき} is fired at lower temperatures and has a warmer, rougher texture, while {磁器|じき} is fired at higher temperatures and is smooth and translucent. Together they are called {陶磁器|とうじき}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {陶器|とうき}{市|いち} (pottery market/fair)
- {陶器|とうき}の{皿|さら} (ceramic plate)
- {陶器|とうき}を{焼|や}く (to fire pottery)

Famous Japanese pottery styles include {有田焼|ありたやき}, {瀬戸焼|せとやき}, {備前焼|びぜんやき}, and {益子焼|ましこやき}.
